capabilities.target: Third-party enrichment API (industry, size, headquarters lookup), billed per call
CRM account record fields (industry, size, headquarters)

inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows (40,000 rows)

instructions.note: 'Keep going until every row is complete' sets no step, retry, or runtime limit, and roughly 3 percent of rows (malformed company names) can never produce a complete result, so the stated goal is structurally unachievable and the instruction gives no stopping condition.

The prompt instructs the agent to retry or spawn a researcher sub-agent on failure with no retry cap and no limit on recursion depth or sub-agent count, and runtime notes confirm sub agents can spawn their own researchers.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota
Sales and marketing tools dependent on the shared enrichment quota

controls.name: Maximum unattended steps and runtime limit
controls.decay_rationale: A hard step/runtime cap enforced by the orchestrator does not depend on model behavior and would not weaken as the model improves, but it is not present in this design.

controls.name: Spend cap / rate limit on enrich.lookup calls
controls.decay_rationale: A spend ceiling enforced outside the model narrows the path regardless of model capability, but no such cap exists today.

controls.name: Sub-agent spawn depth and count limit
controls.decay_rationale: A recursion depth/count limit enforced by the spawning mechanism is independent of model capability, but runtime notes state there is no maximum on sub agents.

controls.name: Retry cap / circuit breaker for rows that cannot be completed
controls.decay_rationale: A circuit breaker that routes permanently-malformed rows to a dead-letter path after N attempts is enforced outside the model and would not decay with model capability, but it is absent here.

controls.name: Spend alert / anomaly detection on the enrichment account
controls.decay_rationale: Detective alerting on spend velocity does not depend on model behavior, but runtime notes explicitly state there is no spend alert.

controls.name: Dedicated quota isolated from sales and marketing
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping the enrichment agent to its own quota, separate from the shared sales/marketing key, is independent of model capability, but the design shares one quota across all three consumers.

findings.title: Unbounded spend loop on shared billed API exhausts a cross-team quota (TC6)

attack_path.note: 40,000-row nightly batch; ~3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete result
Billed per call, no retry cap, no spend cap
Shared monthly quota with sales and marketing; exhausting it disables their tools until next month

evidence.observation: There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.
enrich.lookup is billed per call; the API key and its monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing, whose tools stop working until next month if the quota runs out.
Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000 rows have malformed company names that never return a complete result, so retries on those rows never terminate.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.
'Keep going until every row is complete' supplies no stopping condition even though some rows can never complete.

recommendations.action: Add a hard per-run retry cap and an overall spend cap on enrich.lookup, enforced by the orchestrator rather than by prompt instruction.
Give the enrichment agent its own quota or sub-allocation, isolated from the sales and marketing shared key.
Add real-time spend alerting and an automatic circuit breaker when the enrichment account approaches its quota threshold.
Route rows that fail after N attempts to a dead-letter queue for human review instead of indefinite retry.

findings.title: Unbounded recursive sub-agent spawning has no depth or count limit (ASI08)

attack_path.note: Rows with malformed names repeatedly fail enrichment
Sub-agent spawned to investigate a failing row
Sub-agents can spawn their own researchers with no depth or count limit
Each researcher presumably continues calling the billed lookup, compounding spend

evidence.observation: There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents; sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
The prompt instructs spawning a researcher sub-agent on failure and continuing until every row is complete, with no stated limit on recursion depth or sub-agent count.
3 percent of rows have malformed names that never complete, so researcher sub-agents assigned to those accounts have no natural termination condition and can keep spawning further researchers.

recommendations.action: Enforce a maximum sub-agent spawn depth (e.g., 1, no further delegation) and a maximum total researcher count per run.
Cap aggregate runtime and step budget across the whole batch, including all spawned sub-agents combined, enforced by the orchestrator.
Log and alert on live sub-agent spawn counts so runaway recursion is caught before quota exhaustion.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach an S3 sink (a billed spend action and an unbounded delegate action) from an internal but uncontrolled data source, giving a base tier of high, which is pushed to critical by the autonomy modifier: the agent is A4 fully autonomous, can spawn its own sub-agents, which can themselves spawn further sub-agents, and has no step or runtime ceiling. No control in the design earns rubric credit: every recommended structural control (step/runtime limit, spend cap, recursion limit, retry circuit breaker, spend alert, quota isolation) is absent, so residual equals inherent at critical. There is no forecast-horizon finding because nothing needs to change for this to be exploitable; the 3 percent of rows with malformed names already guarantees, on the very first nightly run, retries and sub-agent spawns that never terminate, so forecast equals residual at critical. The single highest-leverage fix is splitting the enrichment agent onto its own quota and adding an orchestrator-enforced spend cap and spawn-count limit, since the shared, uncapped billed API combined with unbounded recursive delegation is what turns an internal data-quality issue into a cross-team denial of service.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no actual step counts, spend totals, or quota consumption were measured.

No tool manifest, MCP config, or IaC was provided, so exact credential scoping for enrich.lookup and the researcher sub-agent (e.g., whether sub-agents use the same API key) is inferred from the runtime notes rather than verified against configuration, which limits confidence on credential_scope to the design's stated intent.

Attack paths were limited to the toxic-combination search procedure's recommended length; deeper chains of recursive sub-agent spawning beyond two levels are not enumerated individually, though the unbounded nature of the recursion is captured in finding f2.
